evaluator: Independent evaluator; direct Blender reopen/probe plus source snapshot and image inspection

criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: OSM way 301923755 is explicitly named FarmHouse Fraternity, Purdue Chapter and tagged with 1028 State Street; the local source image shows the FarmHouse name sign and brick building.
The candidate building mesh bounds align with the OSM polygon bounds at approximately 27.67 x 38.99 m; the dedicated build script uses that exact outline.

Purdue/Tippecanoe GIS FID 778 is a conflicting authoritative geometry: approximately 29.90 x 21.85 m with 636.39 m² area vs OSM 740.24 m² and only 0.536 axis-aligned bounding-box IoU. The candidate record acknowledges this mismatch.
findings: The conflict cannot be dated or resolved from available evidence: FID 778 exposes no source date and neither source supplies a survey. Calling the GIS polygon historical/partial is not established. Identity is strong, footprint source choice is defensible but uncertain.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: The asset is in campus-coordinate XY (not local-origin coordinates), matching the simple-massing compatibility rule.
Its base footprint is built directly from the OSM way’s campus-local transform and overall mesh bounds include the expected entry/roof projections.
Source conflict leaves exact surveyed dimensions unverified; no independent geodetic control or measured elevation was found.
findings: Plan placement is supported by the OSM named geometry and aligns with the project’s original massing location, but this is not an independent survey check.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: KJG project information supports four stories over a basement; the asset correctly labels overall height as estimated, not measured.

The saved render shows five repeated window rows above the basement/plinth, while the documented program says four stories above basement; build script defines five window bands and five floor-plate levels.

The main roof spans nearly the entire footprint at about 3.1 m rise over half-span about 12.5 m, roughly 14 degrees, and is a single simple gable. Source aerial/project photos show steep, intersecting roof wings and clear gables.
findings: The floor/window stack appears one story too tall relative to the four-story source description. Main roof silhouette and pitch materially disagree with source photos; roof intersections/wings are omitted. Absolute eave/ridge heights remain unverified estimates.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: Brick, limestone bands/quoins, divided sash, white eaves, and an entry portico are recognizable elements visible in the saved source photographs.
Fresh-open render has a repeated brick facade and window grid with material differentiation.

Reference entrance photos show a large white columned porch/portico extending along the facade and around the corner, along with a prominent FarmHouse name sign; the candidate has only a small corner canopy/entry and no sign.
Source photos show materially steeper, articulated roof edges and detailed gable treatment, while the model’s top reads nearly flat from the saved review camera.
findings: Main entry scale and porch footprint are underrepresented; signature FarmHouse sign absent. Window rhythm is generic and appears five rows. Corner quoins are isolated small blocks, unlike the substantial repeated limestone blocks in photos.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Fresh-open in Blender 5.2 succeeds. Scene is Building_massing_farmhouse_fraternity_purdue_chapter_0b8908b; expected Asset_ collection exists.

The asset is compacted into one mesh object with 8,469 vertices and 4,009 polygons; no linked libraries, external images, or missing texture dependencies. Ten procedural material definitions are present.
Building evidence records source providers, URLs, feature IDs, retrieval date, CRS/method, source uncertainty, geometry, and edits.
findings: All surface materials are procedural with no image textures; this is portable but provides no mapped photographic facade detail. The interior is only schematic and is not visible in the exterior-only saved review.

Purdue_Tippecanoe_FID_778.resolution: Unresolved: source date is absent from FID 778 record; available photos corroborate a substantial complex but cannot adjudicate its surveyed outline. Do not label FID 778 historical/partial as a fact.

overall_findings: Strong building identity and evidence-supported placement, but the building fails the 8/10 threshold due to the floor-count/window-row mismatch, roof silhouette, and missing principal porch/signature entrance details.
The OSM outline is a reasonable current-model choice because it is named and matches the original campus massing extents, but the source conflict remains open.
